title: Astro Portal target library query and result
description: GET /api/target-library and GET /v1/targets query parameters and response. Guest browsing never requires a credential; only `favorites=1` does — a web session for the web route, a device bearer for the v1 route. A query with no match still returns the full paginated envelope with an empty `targets` array, never a null or missing field. GET /v1/targets/{targetId} returns one `target` rather than the paginated envelope. Results are ordered by designation unless `sort=planner` asks for the planner's relevance ranking; the response echoes the ordering it applied in `sort`, which a portal predating the parameter omits. The two kinds of entry the application writes itself, the bright stars and the constellations, are ordinary entries of the catalogue (`type=stellar`, `type=constellation`); see `stellar`, `constellationInfo`, `planVisualOnly` and `planExcluded` of the target.

target.description: One catalogue entry. Its presentation fields are the portal's and are deliberately not constrained here; `photoFavorite` and `visualFavorite` are present only when the reader is authenticated.

distance.description: The target's distance, "when known, otherwise absent": `null` when no layer has one. Written at import (`packages/astro-core/src/target-distance.ts`), in this order: `published` (a value from the literature in the curated table, cited with its `reference`), `parallax` (OpenNGC's Gaia parallax, 1/Pax, for a cluster or a nebula with at least 0.5 mas, never for a galaxy), `redshift` (a galaxy at 1 000 km/s or more, Hubble's law at 70 km/s/Mpc: an estimate, which a client writes as such). Additive; a portal predating the field omits it.

lightYears.description: Light-years, rounded to the significant digits of the layer (two for `redshift`, three for `parallax`, the published digits for `published`).

reference.description: `published`: author, year, journal, bibliographic identifier. `parallax` and `redshift`: the OpenNGC column and the rule.

description.description: Only in `GET /v1/targets/{id}` of a bright star or a constellation: its short text (two to four sentences) in the requested `locale`, else in English (`storyFallbackLocale` then says `en`), `null` when none is written. The same text is the target's knowledge text: `story`, `storyParagraphs` (one paragraph) and `storySections` (one opening, no intertitle) carry it, no `spokenParagraphs` is served, and a client shows it, keeps it for offline use and reads it aloud as it does a published page. Absent for any other target.

storyFallbackLocale.description: Present only when the target's knowledge text (`story`, `storyParagraphs`) has no curated text in the requested `locale`: the locale it is shown in instead, the registry's default (`en`). Never a blank text; absent when the text is in the requested locale.

heading.description: The section's intertitle; `null` for the opening, which has none.

storySections.description: Optional. The knowledge text of a published page (the long catalogue texts) cut into its sections, in the language of `story`; the paragraphs of every section, in order, are `storyParagraphs`. Absent for a target whose text is a short generated one: a client then shows `storyParagraphs` as before.

researchSources.description: The links the text stands on, each with the words that name it (for a published page, in the language of the text, with the date it was consulted).

researchNote.description: Optional. The note that closes the sources of a published page (the licences of the sources), in the language of `story`; shown under the sources.

spokenParagraphs.description: Optional. The knowledge text written to be heard, in the requested `locale`, for the read-aloud voice: short sentences, no parenthesis, no catalogue shorthand, numbers and names written as they are said. Present only for a locale with spoken templates and a text in that locale (never beside `storyFallbackLocale`); absent, the reader speaks the written text through its pronunciation lexicon.

childrenSpokenParagraphs.description: Optional. The children's spoken variant, read when the device's children's switch is on: the object's name and its kind, concrete comparisons, no figure that needs a unit lesson. Present only beside `spokenParagraphs`; absent, the reader speaks `spokenParagraphs`.

constellationKey.description: The IAU abbreviation of the constellation that holds the target (`Lyr`, `UMa`, `CrB`), the key of the `constellation` filter; `Système solaire` for the Solar System's bodies. Placed by the IAU boundaries (`constellationAt`) when the source gives none. Additive: a portal predating migration 109 keyed a constellation by its French name.

planVisualOnly.description: True for a bright star (type `Étoile brillante`): never offered by the suggestions nor ranked by `sort=planner`, but may be added to a plan by hand, in visual mode only. Additive; absent from a portal predating the bright stars.

planExcluded.description: True for a constellation (type `Constellation`): never put in a plan, never suggested. Additive; absent from a portal predating the constellations.

isBest.description: In « Essentielles ». Disjoint from `isExtended` since TARGET-SELECTIONS-TAGS-01: a target is in one selection at most.

isExtended.description: In « Étendues », the targets beyond the Essentials (no longer the Essentials too).

modes.description: The modes a target of a selection is proposed in, in this order: `visual` (within reach of a 200 mm telescope under a good sky), `photo`, or both; both for a target of a selection that carries none; empty for a target of no selection. Additive; absent from a portal predating TARGET-SELECTIONS-TAGS-01.

stellar.description: Present for a bright star (type `Étoile brillante`, catalogue `BrightStars`, identifier `star-hip-<Hipparcos number>`; the 92 stars of visual magnitude 2.5 or brighter). The distance is the entry's `distance` (source `parallax`).

properName.description: The proper name; null for a star that has none in common use.

nameKind.description: `iau`: a name of the IAU Catalog of Star Names; `traditional`: a name in common use that the catalogue does not list; null: no proper name.

names.description: The name in each of the ten languages of the application.

distanceIsEstimate.description: True when the parallax is beyond 150 parsecs: the distance's `reference` then begins « Estimation : » and a client writes « estimation » beside it.

epoch.description: The position carries no proper motion.

constellationInfo.description: Present for a constellation (type `Constellation`, catalogue `Constellations`, identifier `constellation-<abbreviation>`). The entry's own `coordinate` is the centre of the smallest circle that holds the stars of its lines. `GET /v1/targets/{id}` adds the two lists `brightStars` and `targets`.

names.description: The name in each of the ten languages of the application.

brightStarCount.description: How many of the 92 bright stars it holds.

targetCount.description: How many of the catalogue's other objects it holds (its bright stars and its own entry left out). In the answers of the catalogue's search.

hasDrawing.description: Whether the western sky culture draws an illustration of it.

brightStars.description: Its bright stars, the brightest first. Only in `GET /v1/targets/{id}`.

targets.description: The catalogue's objects in it, the editorial selection first, then by brightness. Only in `GET /v1/targets/{id}`.

type.description: A type of the catalogue (`Galaxie`…), or `stellar` (the 92 bright stars) or `constellation` (the 88 constellations).

constellation.description: The IAU abbreviation of a constellation (`Lyr`), or any name that names it (`Lyre`, `Lyra`): it filters every type, the bright stars and the constellations included.

selection.description: `best` the Essentials, `extended` the Extended: two disjoint lists.

mode.description: Keeps, of the `selection` asked, the targets proposed in that mode, and counts `counts.best`/`counts.extended` (and `countsUnfiltered`) in it. Without a `selection` the page is not filtered by it: a catalogue is whole. Absent or empty: every target of the selection.

sort.description: Result ordering. Absent or empty means `designation`, the alphabetical catalogue index every client has always received. `notoriety` is the order of the planner's catalogue screens: the editorial selection first (Essentielles, then Étendues, then the rest), then the catalogue's rank (Système solaire, Messier, Caldwell, NGC, IC, Sharpless, Barnard, LBN, Abell, LDN), then the designation; it does not depend on the observer and drops nothing. `planner` applies the web planner's own relevance score (editorial tier, type, brightness, apparent size, and culmination height at `latitude`) and drops targets it cannot rank, so `total` and `counts` describe the ranked set.

latitude.description: Observer latitude for `sort=planner`, in degrees. Only the ranking reads it. Clients send it coarsely — the mobile planner rounds to the whole degree — because the score needs no better and the value travels in the query string.

minimumAltitude.description: Culmination height, in degrees, below which `sort=planner` treats a target as unobservable from `latitude`. Defaults to 30.

listLimit.description: `GET /v1/targets/{targetId}` of a constellation only: how many items each of its two lists holds.

sort.description: The ordering the portal actually applied. Absent from a portal that predates the `sort` parameter, which always orders by designation.

counts.description: The editorial selection dropdown's own faceted counts. Each of `best`/`extended` is computed over targets matching every *other* active filter (`q`, `type`, `constellation`, `catalogue`, `hemisphere`, `season`, a favorites restriction) with the `selection` filter itself ignored, so choosing `selection=best` never changes `extended`'s own count (and vice versa) — the regression this fixes had every one of `total`/`best`/`extended` collapse onto the page's own `selection`-filtered size. `total` is the same facet with no editorial predicate: the count the "All" option represents. The two selections are disjoint, and each count is in the `mode` asked, when one is.

countsUnfiltered.description: Additive (absent from a portal predating this field, which a client then treats as `counts` alone — R7's single-number display). The same three counts as `counts`, with *no* filter applied at all, not even the other dimensions: a fixed `n` for `R7`'s `x/n` display once at least one filter is active (`counts.best` is `x`, `countsUnfiltered.best` is `n`). Constant for a given catalogue revision, independent of `q`/`type`/`constellation`/`catalogue`/`hemisphere`/`season`/`selection`/favorites.

catalogueOptions.description: The catalogue dropdown's own options, always the full set (never shrinking as filters narrow the page) with two counters per entry.

count.description: Faceted: how many targets carry this catalogue among those matching every *other* active filter, the `catalogue` filter itself ignored. A portal predating the fix instead counted this catalogue across the whole, unfiltered library regardless of any other active filter — a different but likewise non-contaminating bug this corrects at the same time.

total.description: Additive (absent from a portal predating this field). This catalogue's count with no filter applied at all — R7's `n`.

typeOptions.description: The type dropdown's own options, following the same `count`/`total` rule as `catalogueOptions` above.

count.description: Faceted: matches among targets satisfying every *other* active filter, the `type` filter itself ignored.

total.description: Additive (absent from a portal predating this field). This type's count with no filter applied at all — R7's `n`.

skyList.description: At most `listLimit` items (default 12, at most 24) and the total.
